task_specification.objective: Make the candidate closure-ready by restoring audible bounded footsteps and ordinary-route victory animation ownership, delivering a playable 25–40-enemy final-wave performance profile, and completing the uninterrupted release run across victory, failure, build, result, credits, and replay surfaces.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by three distinct conditions: footstep authorizations do not reach a native playing source or the Effects/Master mix; victory animation ownership has only been demonstrated through a diagnostic result shortcut instead of the ordinary five-wave transition; and the release profiles remain unqualified because the authored final boss wave admits only five ordinary enemies while the contract requires a representative 25–40-enemy scene, followed by three clean retries and complete ordinary victory/build-route evidence.

stop_conditions: Do not replace or alter the preserved CC0 footstep recording, seven-state Warden package, authored cemetery, HUD family, InputMap, or clean 40-enemy pool; repair their product-owned bindings and lifecycle integration.

Stop and restore the last working boundary if any change breaks native project validation, host boot, ordinary input, automatic combat causality, pause ownership, pool reset, or terminal exactly-once behavior.

Do not claim dense-performance acceptance from llvmpipe, a viewport below 1920x1080, an empty arena, diagnostic-only density, or fewer than three complete Retry cycles; leave the formal verdict to Tester on a representative renderer.
Do not treat diagnostic result or wave selectors as ordinary-route evidence, and keep all validation-only actions editor-guarded and absent from release exports.

Do not claim issue or phase closure from Developer self-validation; stop after the candidate is recapture-ready and Tester has the explicit black-box and white-box matrices needed for formal disposition.

strategy.rationale: Change strategy after repeated treatments: trace the footstep event through stream assignment, native player state, bus routing, and mixed output, then restore a direct bounded playback owner or repair the wrapper at the first failed boundary instead of retuning duration or volume. Preserve the accepted animation mapping and prove victory through the authoritative ordinary boss/run transition rather than another shortcut. Independently make the shipped final boss wave itself satisfy the dense profile, then qualify the full release through ordinary routes and stable lifecycle baselines.

code: Run the frozen `native_godot_project` and `host_godot_boot` checks and require both to remain passing.
Import and parse the project without fatal Godot/GDScript errors, missing resources, invalid signal bindings, or recurring runtime error spam.

Inspect the final audio resource binding and provenance to confirm the accepted footstep recording is intact, Effects and Music buses exist, no generated-tone fallback was added, and release guards exclude validation actions.
Audit project, manifest, provenance, notices, and text resources for private dependencies, credentials, machine-specific absolute paths, missing runtime files, and uncredited external assets.
runtime: Tester recaptures a fresh Title-to-Play physical movement audio sequence on Effects and Master, pairing WAV metrics and source-event timing with Warden displacement, semantic authorizations, active owner count, release, pause, and Retry states.

Tester completes one uninterrupted ordinary 420–600-second victory route and one ordinary failure route, binding wave ids, route kind, build history, boss phases, terminal commit count, Warden victory/Cheer ownership, result fields, Retry, and Title return.

Tester captures the ordinary 1920x1080 final-wave/Bellkeeper profile with 25–40 ordinary enemies, all three weapons, pickups, HUD, animation, VFX, lights, audio, frame-time percentiles, bounded work counters, and renderer identity, then repeats complete reset verification across three cycles.

Tester exercises three separate build shapes through truthful drafts and binds each choice to the next changed combat event and to the final result presentation; diagnostic preparation may shorten branch setup but cannot satisfy ordinary-route or terminal acceptance by itself.
visual: Compare calm and dense gameplay screenshots with the frozen visual reference for the high-angle cemetery framing, warm-lantern/cool-moonlight hierarchy, central arena readability, distinct silhouettes, and compact HUD.
Capture representative dense final-wave and Bellkeeper telegraph frames showing recoverable lanes and visible player, hostile, reward, and boss feedback without obscuration.

Capture the ordinary victory transition with the Warden visibly performing Cheer, followed by the truthful victory result; also capture failure result, clean Retry gameplay, Title, and Credits & Notices at the supported viewport and UI scale.

done_when: A fresh Title-to-Play capture followed by 1.5 seconds of physical movement records at least one native footstep source transition, recognizable output above -55 dBFS on both Effects and Master, and matching semantic authorization without relying on a generated tone or modified source recording.

Each footstep playback retires within 0.28 seconds, movement owns no more than two voices, and release, pause, terminal transition, Retry, and Title return leave zero stale movement owners or duplicated players.

The direct stream/player/bus receipt identifies the intact bound footstep resource, the playing AudioStreamPlayer, Effects routing, start and retirement times, and any bounded rejection; semantic counters alone do not satisfy acceptance.

An ordinary, diagnostic-free five-wave run reaches victory between 420 and 600 seconds, resolves the preserved semantic state `victory` to authored clip `Cheer`, holds terminal animation ownership, commits the result exactly once, and resets to semantic `idle` on ordinary Retry.

Idle, move, dash, cast, hurt, death, and victory remain distinct deformation clips on the preserved Warden hierarchy; no wrapper transform animation, unrelated fallback clip, or package replacement is introduced.
tasks.instructions: Treat the silent footstep as a playback-boundary defect, not another envelope-tuning pass. Compare direct native player restoration, wrapper/binding repair, source replacement, and isolation; preserve the accepted recording and choose the first approach that produces a real source transition and mixed output with bounded ownership. Audit stream assignment, bus existence, player lifecycle, same-frame voice allocation, pause processing, window retirement, and reset ordering. In the same criterion family, retain the existing seven-state Warden profile and make the authoritative ordinary Bellkeeper defeat/run transition expose victory semantic ownership, resolved clip, route kind, commit count, and Retry reset. Add candidate instrumentation only where needed for Tester to bind ordinary black-box behavior to white-box ownership; do not manufacture victory or auto-advance a prepared state.

done_when: The shipped ordinary final Bellkeeper wave sustains 25–40 ordinary enemies alongside the boss, all three equipped weapon families, pickups, HUD, authored animation, VFX, bounded lights, and semantic audio; it does not depend on a diagnostic-only density fixture.

At 1920x1080 on the designated renderer, the representative profile records renderer identity, sample duration/count, p50/p95/p99/worst frame time, physics and high-churn counts; the distribution is consistent with a stable 60 FPS presentation, with p95 no higher than 20 ms and no sustained frame interval above 33.3 ms.

Enemy live count never exceeds 40; neighbor visits remain bounded to 12 candidates per query; telegraph, light, pickup, projectile, effect, audio-voice, and attack-history counts remain within their declared caps without hiding boss warnings or player damage feedback.

Three complete profile-to-Retry cycles return to the same clean baseline on both the immediate and next-frame receipts: zero active enemies, boss, projectiles, pickups, effects, neighbor registrations, Wisp handles/targets, attack ledgers, and effect voices, with a stable 40-enemy pool and no increasing callbacks or recurring errors.

tasks.instructions: Advance the player-facing final wave from its current low supporting-crowd cap to the contract's representative 25–40 ordinary enemies while preserving recoverable movement lanes, Bellkeeper telegraphs, automatic combat legality, and the stable 40-enemy pool. A separate ordinary failure route produces one failure result; victory and failure result pages each truthfully show elapsed time, level, defeated enemies, damage dealt, damage taken, selected upgrades, equipped weapon ranks, and the correct outcome.

Three separate ordinary end-of-run builds demonstrate focused lantern bolts, close Gravespade sweeps, and orbiting Wandering Wisps as visibly and mechanically distinct identities, with truthful draft transactions and observable post-selection changes.

Credits & Notices and ASSET_PROVENANCE account for every external runtime asset and adapted code source; the release contains no private-pool dependency, credential, machine-specific absolute path, reference-only media, debug presentation, or release-enabled validation action.
